summary: André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics who studied under doctoral supervisor August Conrady. He held a post at the University of Leipzig from circa 1912 to 1935.

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, alongside studies at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has taught at Smith College.

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her doctorate at New York University under Alexander C. Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Free University of Berlin and as a researcher at the University of Oulu.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University.

Angela Zito is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago in 1989. Around 1996, she became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University.

Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who completed her Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel, where she held the Lehrstuhl für Praktische Philosophie in 2001.

Angelika Malinar is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed her Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Tübingen. She taught at the Free University of Berlin and SOAS, becoming Professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Angelo Brelich was a scholar of religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University from circa 1931 to 1937 and held a post at the University of Rome from circa 1958 to 1977.

Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Universities of Turin and Berlin, learning under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and the University of Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and later served as director of Sandhaan, which he founded in 1988.

Ankur Barua is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned degrees from Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong, and held an attested post at the University of Delhi in 2012.
Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She held posts at Cornell University and Syracuse University, where she became a professor around 1993.

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and served as professor and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian and anthropologist who studied at Barnard College and Columbia University. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Michigan before chairing the anthropology department at The New School in 2004.

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at the University of Heidelberg and the University of Tübingen. She served as an assistant professor in Indology at the University of Würzburg, attested between 2012 and 2015.

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her Ph.D. at SOAS under Lionel Caplan. In 2002, she became research coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and assistant editor of Bulletin of Tibetology.

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan in 2003, lectured at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" circa 2013, and held a post at the University of Naples Federico II.
